steps.title: Scope the RRA-001 arbiter and trace R1-R11 to MA content
steps.goal: Write the Overview: a zero-latency, N-way (2..32) round-robin arbiter with lock/burst support, a MAX_LOCK bound on locked-continuation cycles, binary index/valid and locked-status outputs, targeting 500 MHz in 7 nm at N=16. Include a requirement-to-section trace table and record the clarifications from Q1-Q3.

spec_evidence.quote: shared-resource arbiter for the on-chip interconnect (up to 32 masters).
The arbiter shall support N requesters, N a parameter in 2..32.
Grant decision shall be made in the same cycle as the request (zero-latency) to avoid bubbles on the interconnect.

options: Purely combinational grant from req/lock plus registered arbitration state
Registered grant (1-cycle latency)
decisions.choice: gnt is computed combinationally in the same cycle from req, lock and registered state (pointer, lock owner, lock counter). No pipeline stage is allowed on req->gnt.
decisions.rationale: R4 requires a zero-latency grant to avoid interconnect bubbles.

done_when: Overview states the function, the N range, the zero-latency property, the lock/MAX_LOCK feature (MAX_LOCK counts continuation cycles only) and the 500 MHz/7 nm/N=16 target
Trace table maps each of R1-R11 to at least one MA section
Overview states that the arbiter is work-conserving, with no idle cycles on lock release or expiry

steps.title: Define the req/lock/gnt/index/valid/locked port list and the N, MAX_LOCK parameters
steps.goal: Fix every port with its width, direction and timing class (combinational output vs registered state), and every parameter with its derived widths.

spec_evidence.quote: The arbiter shall drive a one-hot `gnt[N-1:0]`; at most one bit is set per cycle.
The arbiter shall output the binary index of the granted requester and a valid flag.
The arbiter shall output a status flag indicating the current grant is a locked continuation.
To bound latency, a single lock shall not exceed MAX_LOCK consecutive cycles; MAX_LOCK = 0 means unlimited.

options: No accept/ready input: a grant is consumed in every cycle it is asserted
Add a resource ready/enable input that freezes arbitration state
decisions.choice: No accept/ready input. Every asserted grant counts as a served cycle for pointer and lock-counter updates.
decisions.rationale: The spec lists no such signal, and the zero-latency interconnect context suggests the resource accepts a grant every cycle.
decisions.question: Can the shared resource stall (backpressure)? If so, should the arbiter get a ready/accept input that holds the grant and freezes the round-robin pointer and lock counter?

options: Combinational, same cycle as gnt
Registered (one cycle after gnt)
decisions.choice: gnt_idx (width $clog2(N)), gnt_valid (= |gnt) and gnt_locked are combinational and cycle-aligned with gnt.
decisions.rationale: Registering them would misalign them with the zero-latency grant and make them useless as a same-cycle mux select.
decisions.question: Must the binary grant index, valid flag and locked flag be valid in the same cycle as gnt (combinational), or may they be registered one cycle later?

done_when: Port table lists clk, rst_n, req[N-1:0], lock[N-1:0], gnt[N-1:0], index, valid and the locked flag, with widths and directions
Index width rule is stated for N=2..32, including N that is not a power of 2
MAX_LOCK semantics (number of locked-continuation cycles; burst up to MAX_LOCK+1 grants) and the counter width ($clog2(MAX_LOCK+1)) are stated, with MAX_LOCK=0 meaning no counter
Parameter checks (N in 2..32, MAX_LOCK>=0) are specified as elaboration-time assertions

steps.title: Design the round-robin priority core: pointer register and masked priority encoding
steps.goal: Specify how the next grant is chosen so that the last-granted requester has the lowest priority, using a structure fast enough for N=16 at 500 MHz.

spec_evidence.quote: Arbitration shall be round-robin: after requester i is granted, requester i has the lowest priority in the next arbitration.
A grant shall only be given to a requester whose `req` is asserted in that cycle.
Must close timing at 500 MHz in 7 nm for N=16.

options: Dual priority encoder: thermometer mask of positions above the last grant, masked and unmasked fixed-priority encoders, select masked if non-empty
Rotate -> fixed-priority -> rotate back (barrel shifters)
Parallel-prefix (Kogge-Stone style) find-first-set on doubled request vector
decisions.choice: Dual masked/unmasked fixed-priority encoders with a registered thermometer mask derived from the last granted index. Each find-first is implemented as a log-depth prefix-OR.
decisions.rationale: This avoids barrel shifters on the critical path, has log2(N) depth, and is the standard choice for single-cycle RR at high frequency.
decisions.question: Do you have a preferred round-robin structure (masked dual priority encoder vs rotate/priority/rotate vs other), or is any structure acceptable as long as timing closes?

options: Update pointer to the granted index on every cycle a grant is issued; hold when idle
Update pointer only at the end of a lock or burst
Advance pointer every cycle regardless of grant
decisions.choice: The registered pointer/mask updates to the granted index in every cycle gnt_valid=1, including locked-continuation cycles. It holds its value when no grant is given.
decisions.rationale: This directly implements R5 and the Q2 answer (the former owner is lowest priority after expiry). Holding on idle preserves fairness history.
decisions.question: When no requester is active, should the round-robin pointer hold its last value (default) or reset/advance?

done_when: Equations or pseudo-RTL are given for the mask, the masked request, both encoders, the select and the pointer next-state
It is shown that gnt is one-hot or zero and is a subset of req in every case
A worked N=4 example shows the priority order after each grant

steps.title: Specify lock ownership: lock_req = |(gnt & lock & req), owner override, and same-cycle release when the owner drops req
steps.goal: Define the lock-owner state and its override of the RR core, following the Q1 answer: the lock is honoured only when it is asserted together with gnt and req, and it is released with immediate re-arbitration when the owner drops req.

spec_evidence.quote: A requester may assert `lock[i]` together with `req[i]` while granted to keep the grant in the following cycle (multi-cycle burst / atomic access).
A grant shall only be given to a requester whose `req` is asserted in that cycle.

options: Register lock_active/owner when gnt[i]&req[i]&lock[i]; next cycle grant owner only if req[owner] is still high, else drop the lock and arbitrate normally in that same cycle
Lock forces grant next cycle even if req drops (violates R3)
Combinational lock that holds the grant in the same cycle
decisions.choice: lock_req = |(gnt & lock & req). In cycle t, if lock_req (and the MAX_LOCK limit is not reached), set lock_q and register the owner as the granted index. In cycle t+1, if lock_q and req[owner], grant the owner (overriding RR). Otherwise release the lock and use normal RR in that same cycle, with no idle cycle. A lock[i] without gnt[i], or a lock without req, is ignored.
decisions.rationale: The user's answer to Q1 confirms this behaviour.

done_when: The lock state (lock_q and an owner index or one-hot) is specified with next-state equations using lock_req = |(gnt & lock & req)
The override mux between the lock-owner grant and the RR grant is shown, including the req[owner] qualification
Ignored cases are listed: lock without req, lock from a non-granted requester, and owner dropping req (same-cycle fallback to RR)

steps.title: Define the MAX_LOCK continuation counter: burst of up to MAX_LOCK+1 grants, expiry re-arbitration, no hardware for MAX_LOCK=0
steps.goal: Specify the counter that limits locked-continuation cycles to MAX_LOCK, the forced release at expiry with the former owner at lowest priority, and removal of the logic when MAX_LOCK=0.

spec_evidence.quote: To bound latency, a single lock shall not exceed MAX_LOCK consecutive cycles; MAX_LOCK = 0 means unlimited.
Starvation-free: every requester holding `req` continuously shall be granted within a bounded number of cycles.

options: Count all consecutive grant cycles of the burst including the initial grant
Count only locked-continuation cycles (burst length MAX_LOCK+1)
At expiry, force at least one cycle where the owner cannot be granted
decisions.choice: MAX_LOCK counts only locked-continuation cycles, so a burst is at most MAX_LOCK+1 consecutive grants (one arbitrated cycle plus up to MAX_LOCK continuations). After MAX_LOCK continuations, lock_req is ignored and the next cycle re-arbitrates normally with the former owner at lowest priority. The arbiter is work-conserving: if nobody else requests, the former owner is re-granted through normal RR, and that grant starts a new burst.
decisions.rationale: The user's answer to Q2 settles this. Users who need the limit to include the first cycle set the parameter to L-1.

decisions.topic: Interaction of MAX_LOCK=0 (unlimited) with starvation-freedom R11
options: Guarantee R11 only when MAX_LOCK>0; with MAX_LOCK=0 the bound is conditional on masters releasing lock in finite time
Forbid MAX_LOCK=0 by assertion
Use a hidden internal cap when MAX_LOCK=0
decisions.choice: Allow MAX_LOCK=0 with no counter hardware. Document that R11 then holds only under the assumption that every lock is released in finite time. With MAX_LOCK>0 the wait is bounded. The user stated (N-1)*MAX_LOCK; the MA writer must re-derive the exact bound under the D7 counting, where each other master can hold up to MAX_LOCK+1 cycles, giving (N-1)*(MAX_LOCK+1). The discrepancy must be recorded.
decisions.rationale: The user's answer to Q3 selected this option. The numeric bound must be consistent with the Q2 counting.

done_when: Counter reset, increment (on each locked-continuation grant), clear (on release or new burst) and limit conditions are given as equations

The expiry condition (count == MAX_LOCK blocks the lock_q set) is specified, with a cycle-by-cycle example for MAX_LOCK=3: cycle 0 arbitrated, cycles 1-3 continuations, cycle 4 re-arbitrated, shown both with and without competing requesters
A generate-if that removes the counter when MAX_LOCK=0 is described
The worst-case wait bound formula for MAX_LOCK>0 is derived consistently with continuation-only counting

steps.title: Derive gnt index, valid and locked-continuation status outputs
steps.goal: Specify the one-hot to binary encoder, the valid flag and the locked flag so they are consistent with gnt in every cycle.

spec_evidence.quote: The arbiter shall output the binary index of the granted requester and a valid flag.
The arbiter shall output a status flag indicating the current grant is a locked continuation.

options: Asserted only in cycles where the grant comes from the lock override (not the first cycle of a burst)
Asserted on every cycle of a locked burst, including the first
decisions.choice: The locked flag is high only in cycles where the grant is issued by the lock override (lock_q & req[owner]). It is low on the initial arbitrated grant of a burst, on a re-grant after expiry, and whenever gnt_valid=0. It is therefore high for at most MAX_LOCK consecutive cycles when MAX_LOCK>0.
decisions.rationale: R9 says 'locked continuation', which excludes the initial grant. This matches the continuation-only counting in D7.

done_when: The OR-tree one-hot to binary encoder is specified, and index is defined (e.g. 0) when valid=0
valid = |gnt is stated
The locked flag equation is given and checked against the S5 MAX_LOCK=3 example (high in cycles 1-3 only)

steps.title: Block diagram and 500 MHz critical-path budget for the combinational req->gnt path
steps.goal: Draw the block diagram (mask/pointer regs, dual PE, lock override mux, continuation counter, encoders) and analyse the combinational depth from req/lock inputs to gnt/index outputs at N=16.

spec_evidence.quote: Must close timing at 500 MHz in 7 nm for N=16.
Grant decision shall be made in the same cycle as the request (zero-latency) to avoid bubbles on the interconnect.

decisions.topic: I/O timing budget assumption for the combinational path
options: Assume req/lock come from master flops and gnt/index go to flops, with the arbiter allotted about 50% of the 2 ns cycle
Arbiter owns the full cycle (registered inputs and outputs inside)
Budget supplied by the integrator
decisions.choice: Assume req and lock are launched from flops in the masters and gnt/idx are captured by flops or a mux in the resource. The arbiter's req->gnt and req->idx logic is budgeted at about 1 ns of the 2 ns period.
decisions.rationale: Zero latency makes the arbiter part of an inter-block combinational path, so a budget split must be assumed to evaluate the 500 MHz target.
decisions.question: What portion of the 2 ns cycle (500 MHz) is the arbiter allowed for the combinational req->gnt and req->index path, given that requests come from masters and grants feed the interconnect mux?

done_when: The block diagram shows all registers and combinational blocks with signal flow
The critical path is identified (req -> masked PE -> select -> lock override mux qualified by req[owner] -> gnt -> index), with logic-depth estimates for N=16 and N=32
The lock/expiry control is shown to depend only on registered state plus req[owner], keeping it off the deep path
The statement 'no pipeline stages; all state updates at clock edge from current-cycle grant' is explicit

steps.title: Single-clock domain and active-low asynchronous reset of pointer, lock and counter state
steps.goal: Specify the clock and reset scheme and the reset value of every state element.

spec_evidence.quote: Single clock, active-low asynchronous reset.

options: Async assert on rst_n low; deassertion assumed synchronised externally
Integrate a reset synchroniser inside the arbiter
decisions.choice: All state flops use async active-low reset (always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)). Synchronous deassertion is the integrator's responsibility; no internal synchroniser is added.
decisions.rationale: R10 fixes an async active-low reset. Reset synchronisers are normally provided at SoC level.
decisions.question: Is rst_n already synchronised on deassertion at SoC level, or should the arbiter include its own reset synchroniser?

done_when: Reset values are listed for the pointer/mask (e.g. requester 0 highest priority), lock_q, owner and the continuation counter
It is stated that after reset with lock_q=0, gnt follows pure RR, and that gnt=0, valid=0 and locked=0 hold whenever req=0
The single clock is confirmed, with no CDC

steps.title: Enumerate corner cases: lock edge cases, MAX_LOCK expiry and re-grant, N extremes and the starvation bound
steps.goal: Document behaviour for every unusual input combination and prove the starvation bound under continuation-only MAX_LOCK counting.

spec_evidence.quote: Starvation-free: every requester holding `req` continuously shall be granted within a bounded number of cycles.
A requester may assert `lock[i]` together with `req[i]` while granted to keep the grant in the following cycle (multi-cycle burst / atomic access).
The arbiter shall support N requesters, N a parameter in 2..32.

done_when: Cases covered: all req low; single requester; all requesters; lock without req; lock from a non-granted master; owner drops req while lock_q=1 (same-cycle RR fallback); expiry with others requesting (owner lowest priority); expiry with sole requester (immediate re-grant, new burst, locked flag low); lock asserted on the expiry cycle; MAX_LOCK=1; N=2; N=32; non-power-of-2 N
The starvation bound is derived for MAX_LOCK>0 with bursts of up to MAX_LOCK+1, and the MAX_LOCK=0 caveat is linked to D8
It is stated that there are no illegal-input error outputs; illegal combinations are ignored

steps.title: Verification plan: reference model, SVA for one-hot/R3/RR/lock rules/continuation bound, and parameter sweep
steps.goal: Define how the MA will be verified against R1-R11 and the Q1-Q3 clarifications.

spec_evidence.quote: at most one bit is set per cycle.
after requester i is granted, requester i has the lowest priority in the next arbitration.
a single lock shall not exceed MAX_LOCK consecutive cycles

done_when: Assertions are listed: $onehot0(gnt); gnt subset of req; valid==|gnt; idx matches gnt; locked flag implies previous-cycle lock_req for the same owner; consecutive locked cycles <= MAX_LOCK (burst <= MAX_LOCK+1) when MAX_LOCK>0; no idle cycle when req!=0 (work-conserving); RR order; bounded wait
A cycle-accurate reference model with a scoreboard is described
Directed tests for every S9 corner case are listed

A parameter sweep is listed: N in {2,3,16,31,32} x MAX_LOCK in {0,1,4}, plus a formal bounded proof for small N; for MAX_LOCK=0 the bounded-wait property is proven under an assume of finite lock duration
Coverage goals include each requester granted, lock expiry hit, lock released early by dropped req, and sole-requester re-grant after expiry

steps.title: Record assumptions and open questions (backpressure, output timing, RR structure, idle pointer, timing budget, reset sync, R7/R11 caveat)
steps.goal: Collect every remaining defaulted decision and record the resolved clarifications from Q1-Q3 so the spec author can confirm them.
